checks.prompt: What is i squared, where i is the imaginary unit?

e^iπ equals −1..why: Euler's identity, e^iπ + 1 = 0, is one of the most quoted equations in mathematics; it is stated directly, in several written forms, hundreds of times in Dolma and has its own Wikipedia article. A model holds it as a stored fact; it can also be worked out from Euler's formula at x = π, but the identity itself is what text states.

sources.quote: In mathematics, Euler's identity (also known as Euler's equation) is the equality
sources.note: The equality that follows in the article is e^{iπ} + 1 = 0.

notes: Delete of replace-0013's original fact (Euler's identity; stored, very_unlikely). Mathematics leaves out worlds (README, Shape per topic): a fact about a number or a shape rests on definitions and proofs, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between. Derived queries ask what the edit forces through the definitions, holding the definitions fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. Every derived query goes through the deleted value of e^iπ and expects 'does not know'. The transitivity queries are rephrased around the original value −1 (i² and (−1)³ instead of i⁴ and cos 0). Risk: Euler's formula at x = π re-derives −1; that is the same proposition in general form, so a model answering −1 has not removed the fact (the same stance as delete-0002 on the incommensurable diagonal).
